title: Intermediate Representations and Optimisation
description: SSA, dataflow, and the passes that change the program without changing what it means.

sourceReferences.title: Stanford CS143
sourceReferences.notes: IR and local/global optimization after the front-end exists.

sourceReferences.title: CMU 15-411/611 Compiler Design
sourceReferences.notes: IR and dataflow as the intellectual center.

sourceReferences.title: LLVM Language Reference Manual
sourceReferences.notes: SSA, φ-nodes, and IR well-formedness as a contract.

modules.title: IR shapes
learningObjectives: Name values so each assignment happens once
Split a program into blocks and edges

modules.title: Dataflow
learningObjectives: Compute a fact that flows until it settles
Say which values are still needed

modules.title: Transformations
learningObjectives: Replace a call with a body only when the price is worth it

concepts.name: Three-address code
concepts.summary: One operator, a few operands, easy to move.
objectives: Rewrite a nested expression into three-address instructions with temporary names
Explain why one operator and a few operands make later motion easy

concepts.name: Control-flow graphs
concepts.summary: Basic blocks and the edges between them.
objectives: Split three-address code into basic blocks and the edges between them
Identify a basic block as a straight-line sequence with one entry and one exit

concepts.name: SSA form
concepts.summary: Single assignment so dataflow becomes a graph problem.
objectives: Rewrite assignments so each name is defined exactly once
Explain why a single definition per name turns use-def into a graph walk

concepts.name: φ-nodes
concepts.summary: A merge of names at a join point.
objectives: Place a φ at a join so one name records which predecessor's value arrives
Predict the φ operands for a variable assigned on two incoming edges

concepts.name: Memory to registers
concepts.summary: Promoting allocas so SSA can see them.
objectives: Promote an alloca that never escapes into an SSA value
Name a reason a stack slot must stay in memory instead of becoming a register

concepts.name: IR verification
concepts.summary: Types and dominance as a checker, not a hope.
objectives: Check that every use is dominated by its definition and that types agree
Diagnose an ill-formed SSA fragment the verifier should reject

concepts.name: Dataflow analysis
concepts.summary: Facts that flow forward or backward until they settle.
objectives: Describe a dataflow fact as something that flows until a fixed point
Predict whether a given analysis must run forward or backward

concepts.name: Liveness
concepts.summary: Which values are still needed.
objectives: Compute which names are live on entry to a short block
Predict why a value that is never used is not live

concepts.name: Alias analysis
concepts.summary: May these two pointers be the same.
objectives: Decide whether two pointers may designate the same location
Name a transformation that becomes illegal if they may alias

concepts.name: Call graphs
concepts.summary: Who might call whom.
objectives: Build a call graph from the calls that might execute
Predict how an indirect call makes the graph conservative

concepts.name: Pass managers
concepts.summary: Order, invalidation, and why passes fight.
objectives: Explain why one pass can invalidate another pass's analysis
Predict a safe order when a transform dirties SSA or alias facts

concepts.name: Constant folding
concepts.summary: Doing arithmetic the compiler can already see.
objectives: Replace an operator whose operands are already constants with the result
State why folding 2+3 does not change observable behavior

concepts.name: Dead code elimination
concepts.summary: Deleting what nothing uses.
objectives: Delete an instruction whose result is not live
Predict when a store cannot be deleted even if its value looks unused

concepts.name: Common-subexpression elimination
concepts.summary: Computing a thing once.
objectives: Reuse an earlier computation of the same expression when values have not changed
Diagnose when two similar expressions are not actually common

concepts.name: Inlining
concepts.summary: Replacing a call with the body, for a price.
objectives: Replace a call with the callee body and state the compile-time price
Predict a case where inlining is legal but unprofitable

concepts.name: Loop-invariant code motion
concepts.summary: Hoisting work the loop does not change.
objectives: Hoist a computation the loop does not change to the preheader
Identify the loop-invariant pattern a pass looks for

concepts.name: LICM carefully
concepts.summary: When a load is not actually invariant.
objectives: Refuse to hoist a load that may alias a store in the loop
Diagnose a hoist that would change which exception or fault is observed

concepts.name: Strength reduction
concepts.summary: A multiply becoming an add.
objectives: Replace an induction multiply with an add that steps the same sequence
State why the new recurrence still computes the original values

concepts.name: Scalar replacement of aggregates
concepts.summary: Exploding a struct into pieces SSA can eat.
objectives: Split an aggregate into scalar pieces SSA can name
Predict when a field still cannot be promoted because its address escapes

concepts.name: Tail calls
concepts.summary: A call that can be a jump.
objectives: Rewrite a call in tail position as a jump that reuses the current frame
Diagnose a call that is not tail because work remains after it returns

concepts.name: Vectorization
concepts.summary: One instruction, many loop iterations.
objectives: Pack consecutive independent iterations into one SIMD instruction
Name a dependence or alias fact that makes vectorization illegal

concepts.name: Interprocedural optimization
concepts.summary: Facts that cross function boundaries.
objectives: Propagate a fact across a call boundary the inliner has not removed
Compare a local fact with one that is only true after seeing the callee
